prompt: Photorealistic interior of a medieval 14th-century harbourmaster's office in a Hanseatic port town, at eye level. A dim, dark room: heavy soot-blackened oak ceiling beams, rough stone walls with patchy flaking lime plaster, worn wide oak floorboards, deep-set window with small leaded diamond-shaped panes in thick stone, one casement swung open. Outside the window a bright foggy morning: pale grey fog with faint silhouettes of tall wooden ship masts, yards and rigging. Cold daylight from the window is the main light, the rest of the room falls into deep shadow. Seen from a corner of the room, the window on the far wall to the right, a low stone hearth with dying embers on the left wall glowing orange. A long trestle table with an open ledger, tally sticks, a set of brass scales and coins, a candle in an iron holder. Barrels and sacks stacked by the wall, a faded painted shield, a ship's model on a shelf. Dust in the light beam. Moody, low-key lighting, realistic aged materials, cinematic 35mm photograph, no people.
